rationale: Untrusted path text is passed directly to Path.of and Files.readString without a trusted-root containment check.
assumptions: NTK_H7_PATH_A is attacker-controlled in the evaluation threat model, load() is invoked, and the process can read at least one file outside the intended root.

rationale: Untrusted path text is passed directly to Path.of and Files.readAllBytes without containment to an authorized root.
assumptions: NTK_H7_PATH_B is attacker-controlled, load() is invoked, and the process can read outside the intended root.

rationale: An attacker-controlled path is resolved against a nominal root but there is no normalization plus startsWith containment check before reading.
assumptions: NTK_H7_PATH_C is attacker-controlled, the application intends confinement under /srv/ntk/data, and load() is invoked.

rationale: The path passed to Files.readString is a fixed literal and has no attacker-controlled path component in this testcase.
assumptions: Assess CWE-22 only; the fixed filesystem path, mounts, and symlinks are trusted and not attacker-modifiable.

rationale: The candidate path is normalized and rejected unless it remains under the normalized trusted root before the read.
assumptions: The trusted root and descendants are not attacker-controlled symlinks or mounts; assess lexical path traversal under the declared root boundary.

rationale: The external filename is restricted to a single safe filename component ending in .txt before resolution under a fixed trusted root.
assumptions: The trusted root and filesystem metadata are not attacker-controlled; the regex check executes exactly as shown and load() is invoked.

rationale: Attacker-controlled command text is supplied to /bin/sh -c, explicitly requesting shell interpretation.
assumptions: NTK_H7_CMD_A is attacker-controlled, /bin/sh exists, and launch() is invoked.

rationale: Attacker-controlled command text is supplied to /bin/bash -c, explicitly requesting shell interpretation.
assumptions: NTK_H7_CMD_B is attacker-controlled, /bin/bash exists, and launch() is invoked.

rationale: The complete command string passed to Runtime.exec is attacker-controlled, allowing selection of the executable and arguments under the stated boundary.
assumptions: NTK_H7_CMD_C is attacker-controlled, launch() is invoked, and the process is permitted to start an attacker-selected executable. This claim does not rely on shell metacharacter interpretation.

rationale: The command is a fixed absolute executable path with no external command text.
assumptions: Assess CWE-78 only; /usr/bin/true and the process environment are trusted and not attacker-replaceable.

rationale: The executable and argument array are fixed literals with no attacker-controlled command material.
assumptions: Assess CWE-78 only; /usr/bin/printf and the process environment are trusted.

rationale: External text is passed only as a data argument to a fixed executable in an argument array; no shell interpreter is invoked.
assumptions: Assess CWE-78 OS command injection only; /usr/bin/printf is trusted and does not interpret the value as a command. Separate option/argument injection concerns are outside this testcase.

rationale: Decoded query text is concatenated into an HTML text context and written as text/html without HTML encoding.
assumptions: The request query is attacker-controlled, getQuery() supplies decoded query text, the response is rendered as HTML, and handle() is invoked.

rationale: Decoded query text is concatenated directly into a double-quoted HTML attribute without attribute encoding.
assumptions: The request query is attacker-controlled and can contain characters that terminate the quoted attribute after URI decoding; the response is rendered as HTML.

rationale: Decoded query text is embedded directly inside a JavaScript string in an HTML script block without JavaScript or HTML context encoding.
assumptions: The request query is attacker-controlled and can contain quote/script-breaking characters after decoding; the response is rendered as HTML and script execution is permitted.

rationale: The helper encodes ampersand and angle brackets before the value is inserted into a normal HTML text node.
assumptions: Only this straight-line HTML text context is assessed; there is no later decoding or unsafe DOM reinsertion and esc() behaves exactly as shown.

rationale: Attacker-controlled query text is returned as text/plain rather than embedded into an HTML document by this handler.
assumptions: The client honors text/plain UTF-8 and no downstream component rewrites the response as HTML; assess reflected XSS only.

rationale: The helper encodes ampersand, angle brackets, double quotes, and apostrophes before insertion into a quoted HTML attribute.
assumptions: Only this quoted attribute context is assessed; there is no later decoding or unsafe DOM reinsertion and escAttr() behaves exactly as shown.

rationale: Attacker-controlled text is concatenated into SQL grammar and the resulting statement is executed directly.
assumptions: NTK_H7_SQL_A is attacker-controlled, search() is invoked, and the JDBC driver/database accept an input that can alter the intended predicate.

rationale: Attacker-controlled text is concatenated into the SQL passed to prepareStatement, and that constructed statement is subsequently executed.
assumptions: NTK_H7_SQL_B is attacker-controlled, search() is invoked, and the JDBC implementation executes the SQL text constructed before preparation.

rationale: Attacker-controlled text is formatted into quoted SQL grammar and the resulting SQL string is executed with Statement.executeQuery.
assumptions: NTK_H7_SQL_C is attacker-controlled, search() is invoked, and the database accepts a value that can alter the intended predicate.

rationale: The SQL grammar is fixed with a parameter marker and the external value is bound separately with setString before execution.
assumptions: A trusted conforming JDBC driver preserves parameter binding semantics; the shown statement is not later rebuilt by concatenation.

rationale: The SQL passed to executeQuery is a fixed literal with no external data.
assumptions: Assess CWE-89 only; the Statement/JDBC implementation is trusted and the shown literal is the entire executed SQL text.

rationale: External input selects between two fixed SQL literals but is not inserted into either SQL string.
assumptions: Assess SQL injection only; the JDBC implementation is trusted and no downstream concatenation modifies the selected fixed query.
